Zimmah
ZIM-mah
n. (proper, a Gershonite Levite; Hebrew, a plan or device)
Hebrew Zimmah, a plan, a purpose, and in most other places a wicked device — the word Leviticus uses for the gravest sins. As a personal name it stands for purpose without the pejorative sense.

Biblical Definition

He is placed in the line of Gershom, Levi's eldest son: “Of Gershom; Libni his son, Jahath his son, Zimmah his son” (1 Chronicles 6:20), and again in the pedigree of Ethan the singer, reckoned upward: “The son of Ethan, the son of Zimmah, the son of Shimei” (1 Chronicles 6:42). His name appears a third time in the roll of Levites who arose at Hezekiah's summons to cleanse the temple, as the father of Joah: among those who came were “of the Gershonites; Joah the son of Zimmah, and Eden the son of Joah” (2 Chronicles 29:12). The Gershonites carried the curtains, the coverings and the hangings of the tabernacle through the wilderness, work as necessary and as unglamorous as the Kohathites' charge over the holy vessels was honoured. The divisions of Levi are set out in Scripture with care, because God assigns particular service to particular families.

Origin & Era

Webster (1828) has no entry for this proper name; Scripture fixes it as a Levite of the line of Gershom, and father of Joah in Hezekiah's reformation.

GERSHONITE, n. A descendant of Gershon the eldest son of Levi; charged in the wilderness with the curtains and coverings.

DEVICE, n. That which is formed by design; a scheme; a project; an invention; contrivance.

TABERNACLE, n. A tent; in Scripture, the movable sanctuary of Israel in the wilderness.

CHARGE, n. That which is committed to the care or management of another; trust; custody.

DIVISION, n. The act of dividing; a part separated from the rest; a portion; a section.

Modern Corruption

Service in the church is treated as a matter of preference and availability, where the Levitical divisions show God assigning particular work to particular houses and holding them to it.

expand to see more

This entry faces no significant postmodern redefinition. The principle in Zimmah's line is the ordering of service. Numbers 3 and 4 divide Levi into three houses with three charges: Kohath bore the ark and the vessels, Gershon the curtains and coverings and hangings, Merari the boards, bars, pillars and sockets. Nobody chose his own load, and nobody carried another's. Paul's account of the body works the same way — God hath set the members every one of them in the body, as it hath pleased him — and the health of a congregation depends on members doing their own work rather than the work they would prefer.

There is a warning attached to the Gershonite charge that the name makes pointed. Zimmah elsewhere means a wicked device, a purpose formed against God, and Kohath's house had already shown in Korah what happens when a Levite decides his assigned service is beneath him. The cure for discontent with a small charge is not a larger one but the recognition that the curtains had to be carried, that God appointed who would carry them, and that centuries later a son of that house rose first when a king called the Levites to sanctify the temple.

Greek & Hebrew Roots

Hebrew Zimmah (H2155), a plan or device; zamam (H2161), to purpose; Gereshom (H1648), Gershom; mishmereth (H4931), a charge or watch.

expand to see more

Hebrew Zimmah (H2155) — Zimmah; a plan or purpose, used as a personal name.

Hebrew zamam (H2161) — to devise, to purpose; the root of the word.

Hebrew Gereshom (H1648) — Gershom, a stranger there; Levi's eldest son.

Hebrew mishmereth (H4931) — a charge, a watch, an appointed duty; the Levitical word.

Hebrew yeriyah (H3407) — a curtain; the Gershonite burden through the wilderness.

Usage

"“Libni his son, Jahath his son, Zimmah his son” — the line of Gershom."

"“Joah the son of Zimmah” — among the Levites who arose for Hezekiah."

"“The curtains of the tabernacle” — the charge of his house."
